story: The dove and the olive leaf (SERIES.md episode 10; arc 3, The Flood)

beats: structure bible-story-short (script.beats): cold_open s-voice (God's Genesis 8:16, voice-over: go forth of the ark, laid over the dawn on Ararat as a flash-forward); stake and open loop (months of waiting, nothing but water: when can they leave?); escalation in three rising steps of the waters against the family's hope, each ending on a hook (God remembers, the ark rests on Ararat but still only water; the raven never returns and the dove finds no rest; seven days more, the olive leaf); climax s-release and s-empty-sky (the dove does not come back) carrying Genesis 8:12; payoff (Genesis 8:13: the ground is dry, yet the door stays shut until God speaks); keeper_close (insight: the God who shut the door opened it; comment question; part 11).

narration.text: One day God would say those words. But first came months of waiting: eight people shut inside, and outside nothing but grey water to every horizon.
And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;
Remembered. Not because God had forgotten them, but because the next move was His. A strong wind began to blow across the water, for months, while even the tops of the mountains stayed hidden.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
The ark scraped rock and stopped. But when they looked out, there was still nothing but water, stretching away on every side.
And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made:
First he sent out a raven. It flew off over the water, and it never came back to him.
Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark,
He reached out his hand and drew her back in. Still only water. Still no place to land.
Seven more days. Then he let her go again, and the whole family watched the sky until evening.
And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
One green leaf. Somewhere out there, something was growing again. Seven days later, he opened his hands one more time.
And he stayed yet other seven days; and sent forth the dove; which returned not again unto him any more.
She never came back. And that silence was the best news of all: the dove had found a home on the earth.
and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dry.
Dry ground at last. And still the door stayed shut, because the One who had closed it had not yet said a word.
Most miss this: Noah saw dry ground and still did not walk out. He waited until God said go. The God who shut the door was the God who opened it.
What are you waiting for God to open right now? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part eleven tomorrow: The rainbow.
